qe:
Select the part that contains an error:
'The environment (A) / of the city (B) / is much more (C) / healthier than before (D).'
qh:
उस भाग का चयन करें जिसमें त्रुटि है:
'The environment (A) / of the city (B) / is much more (C) / healthier than before (D).'
e: Avoid Double Comparatives. 'Healthier' is already a comparative degree, so 'more' is redundant. Use 'much' for emphasis, but not 'more healthier'.

qe: The doctor said to the patient, 'Take these medicines twice a day for a week and come for a follow-up next Monday.'
qh: The doctor said to the patient, 'Take these medicines twice a day for a week and come for a follow-up next Monday.'
oe: The doctor told the patient take these medicines
The doctor asked the patient to take those medicines
The doctor advised the patient to take those medicines twice a day for a week and go for a follow-up the following Monday
The doctor advised the patient to take these medicines
oh: The doctor told the patient take these medicines
The doctor asked the patient to take those medicines
The doctor advised the patient to take those medicines twice a day for a week and go for a follow-up the following Monday
The doctor advised the patient to take these medicines
e: 'Advised' is appropriate for doctors. 'These' changes to 'those', 'come' changes to 'go', and 'next Monday' changes to 'the following Monday'.

qe: 'In spite of the heavy rains, the match ______ to its logical conclusion.'
qh: 'In spite of the heavy rains, the match ______ to its logical conclusion.'
e: 'Went on' means continued. The match continued despite the weather.

qe: 'A small room in a big house, hotel, or ship where glasses, dishes, and food are kept.'
qh: 'बड़े घर, होटल या जहाज का वह छोटा कमरा जहाँ बर्तन और भोजन रखा जाता है।'
e: Pantry is the specific word for a room where provisions and kitchenware are stored.

qe: 'If I <u>had realized</u> that the road was so slippery, I would not have driven so fast.'
qh: 'If I <u>had realized</u> that the road was so slippery, I would not have driven so fast.'
e: This is a Third Conditional sentence (If + had + V3, would have + V3). The sentence is grammatically correct.

qe: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word: 'EPHEMERAL'
e: Ephemeral means lasting for a very short time. Transitory (क्षणभंगुर) is the synonym.

qe: Select the most appropriate antonym of the word: 'GREGARIOUS'
e: Gregarious means fond of company; sociable. Reserved (अंतर्मुखी) is the opposite.
To accidentally or prematurely reveal a secret.

qe: 'The storm has severely damaged the coastal villages.'
qh: 'The storm has severely damaged the coastal villages.'
oe: The coastal villages were severely damaged
The coastal villages had been damaged
The coastal villages are being damaged
The coastal villages have been severely damaged by the storm
oh: The coastal villages were severely damaged
The coastal villages had been damaged
The coastal villages are being damaged
The coastal villages have been severely damaged by the storm
e: Present Perfect (has/have + V3) changes to 'has/have + been + V3'.

qe: 'The reason (A) / why he failed (B) / was because (C) / he didn't study (D).'
qh: 'The reason (A) / why he failed (B) / was because (C) / he didn't study (D).'
e: Avoid redundancy. 'The reason why' should be followed by 'that', not 'because'.

qh: गलत वर्तनी वाले शब्द का चयन करें।
e: The correct spelling is Millennium (double 'n').
For execution (legal death), the past participle is 'hanged'. 'Hung' is used for objects like pictures.
To make someone extremely irritated or angry.

qe: 'Either of the (A) / two paths (B) / lead to (C) / the same destination (D).'
qh: 'Either of the (A) / two paths (B) / lead to (C) / the same destination (D).'
e: 'Either of', 'Neither of', 'Each of' always take a singular verb. Correct: 'leads to'.

oe: A novel is read by her
A novel was read by her
A novel is being read by her
oh: A novel is read by her
A novel was read by her
A novel is being read by her
e: Continuous tense adds 'being'.
Exodus means a mass departure. Arrival (आगमन) is the opposite.

qe: 'A person who is recoverning from an illness.'
qh: 'वह व्यक्ति जो बीमारी से ठीक हो रहा हो।'
e: Convalescent is the correct term for recovery phase.
'Prefer' is followed by the preposition 'to'.

qe: He said, 'I have been working since morning.'
qh: He said, 'I have been working since morning.'
oe: He said that he had been working since morning
He said that he has been working
oh: He said that he had been working since morning
He said that he has been working
e: Present Perfect Continuous changes to Past Perfect Continuous.

qe: 'The old man is ______ weak to walk.'
qh: 'The old man is ______ weak to walk.'
e: 'Too...to' structure indicates inability.
Imperative passive: 'Let + obj + be + V3'.
Meager means very small amount. Scanty is the synonym.

qe: 'He was (A) / very tired (B) / so he (C) / laid down (D).'
qh: 'He was (A) / very tired (B) / so he (C) / laid down (D).'
e: Confusing verbs. Past of 'Lie' (recline) is 'lay'. 'Laid' is the past of 'Lay' (put something down). Correct: 'lay down'.
A task that is very easy to accomplish.
Jewellery is the British English standard (Double L).
Vigilant means alert/watchful. Careless is the opposite.
'Take pride in' is a fixed idiom. (However, 'proud of' is used).
Illegible is the term for unreadable writing.

qe: 'No sooner had he arrived <u>when</u> it started raining.'
qh: 'No sooner had he arrived <u>when</u> it started raining.'
e: The pair for 'No sooner' is always 'than'.

qe: 'If I was him (A) / I would not (B) / accept (C) / the gift (D).'
qh: 'If I was him (A) / I would not (B) / accept (C) / the gift (D).'
e: Subjunctive mood for hypothetical cases. Use 'If I were he'.

qe: He said to me, 'What are you doing?'
qh: He said to me, 'What are you doing?'
oe: He asked me what I was doing
He told me what am I doing
He asked me what was I doing
oh: He asked me what I was doing
He told me what am I doing
He asked me what was I doing
e: Indirect question becomes assertive. 'Are doing' changes to 'was doing'.
'M.A.' starts with a vowel sound ('Em'), so use 'an'.
To feel slightly sick or ill.

oe: The match has been won by them
oh: The match has been won by them
e: Present Perfect passive: 'has been + V3'.
Abundant means existing in large quantities. Plentiful is the synonym.
